policy: Opus+Sonnet agreement; a fresh blind Opus pass adjudicates disagreement

reasons.opus: Accepts that the cost barrier is removed and raises a countervailing cost: service cuts.
reasons.sonnet: Grants the barrier removal and raises a countervailing service-cut cost.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Countervailing cost of service cuts; does not deny the barrier is removed.

reasons.opus: Raises a countervailing cost (regressive funding) without denying the barrier is removed.
reasons.sonnet: Raises a separate funding cost rather than disputing barrier removal.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Countervailing cost from regressive funding.

reasons.opus: Says that for already-exempt residents, no financial barrier is actually removed.
reasons.sonnet: Accepts barrier concept but says abolition adds no benefit for already-exempt residents.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Says no barrier is removed for residents who already ride free.

reasons.opus: Names a separate barrier (overcrowding) as a countervailing cost.
reasons.sonnet: Independent overcrowding cost.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Countervailing cost from overcrowding.

reasons.opus: For these residents, the fare is not what blocks access, which narrows the claim.
reasons.sonnet: Points to other access barriers, not denying the fare barrier.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: For these residents the fare was not the barrier, so the claim is overstated.

reasons.opus: The financial barrier remains for these residents, so the claim is overstated.
reasons.sonnet: Independent additional cost barrier.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Other costs remain, so the claim that fare removal enables access is overstated.

reasons.opus: Denies that revenue losses often force cuts and notes that service sometimes expands.
reasons.sonnet: Says cities often expand rather than cut service.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Denies that revenue loss forces cuts where subsidies fill the gap.

reasons.opus: Offers a separate harm (overcrowding) instead of addressing the cuts claim.
reasons.sonnet: Adds a different degradation mechanism, not disputing the claim.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Gives a separate reason access worsens, not a challenge to the claim.

reasons.opus: Lower collection costs shrink the funding gap, which challenges the claim that losses force cuts.
reasons.sonnet: Argues the funding gap forcing cuts is smaller than claimed.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Lower collection costs shrink the revenue gap said to force cuts.

reasons.opus: Says cuts fall first on suburban routes, not low-income ones.
reasons.sonnet: Says cuts typically fall on wealthier suburban routes, not low-income ones.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Denies that cuts fall on low-income routes.

reasons.opus: Weighs a countervailing benefit (net access gain) against the cuts.
reasons.sonnet: Grants cuts but says access still gains overall.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Grants some cuts but says the net access gain from removing the barrier still holds.

reasons.opus: Says safeguards protect low-income routes from cuts.
reasons.sonnet: Says equity reviews protect low-income routes from cuts.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Says equity reviews protect low-income routes from cuts.

reasons.opus: Suggests a different policy design rather than disputing the claim or its link to the parent.
reasons.sonnet: Says cuts are avoidable, contradicting that revenue loss forces them.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Proposes a different policy design.

reasons.opus: Accepts the cases but says they are not representative, so they do not show cuts happen often.
reasons.sonnet: Says not inevitable but doesn't deny that several cities had this outcome.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Grants the cases but denies they generalize to cuts happening 'often'.

reasons.opus: Disputes the claimed cause: other factors may explain the cuts.
reasons.sonnet: Challenges the causal link from surges to route cuts.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Disputes that the surge caused the cuts.

reasons.opus: Even if service is redistributed, it may not worsen access for low-income riders.
reasons.sonnet: Grants redistribution but says it doesn't worsen poor-area access.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Grants the shift but denies it necessarily worsens access.

reasons.opus: Gives counterexamples where no route cuts were documented.
reasons.sonnet: Cites cities with no documented cuts.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Counterexample where no cuts followed.

reasons.opus: Independent point about boarding efficiency.
reasons.sonnet: Argues capacity can absorb riders so overcrowding and cuts needn't occur.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Independent efficiency benefit.

reasons.opus: Ridership growth may not mean overcrowding, which challenges the claim's premise.
reasons.sonnet: Says ridership growth doesn't show overcrowding.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Disputes that the surge meant overcrowding.

reasons.opus: Addresses fare revenue loss (the parent), not the overcrowding claim.
reasons.sonnet: Says service may be preserved without added funding.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Independent cost-saving reason about the parent.

reasons.opus: Questions whether the observed association is valid evidence, not whether studies report it.
reasons.sonnet: Measurement error undermines what the studies show about the curve.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Measurement error weakens the causal inference, not the reported association.

reasons.opus: Disputes that the findings are consistent across cohorts.
reasons.sonnet: Says consistency across cohorts isn't established.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Disputes consistency across cohorts.

reasons.opus: Confounding means the association may not show a causal benefit.
reasons.sonnet: Confounding explains the association rather than causal effect.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Confounding breaks the link from association to causation.

reasons.opus: Disputes that the evidence covers diverse populations.
reasons.sonnet: Says populations aren't actually diverse enough.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Disputes 'across diverse populations'.

reasons.opus: Reverse causation breaks the causal inference.
reasons.sonnet: Reverse causation explains association without supporting benefit.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Reverse causation undermines the causal link.

reasons.opus: A methodological bias weakens the association as evidence.
reasons.sonnet: Bias produces the pattern, weakening its support.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Analytic artifact undermines the inference.

reasons.opus: Says the apparent consistency is overstated.
reasons.sonnet: Says consistency is overstated due to selective reporting.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Says the consistency is overstated.

reasons.opus: Detection bias could produce the association without a real effect.
reasons.sonnet: Detection bias could produce the pattern spuriously.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Detection bias explains the association without causation.

reasons.opus: Says intake is measured reasonably accurately.
reasons.sonnet: Says self-report validates well, so error is not severe.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Says intake measurement is reasonably accurate.

reasons.opus: Even granting imprecision, it would not create a spurious inverse trend.
reasons.sonnet: Grants imprecision but says it can't explain the trend.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Grants imprecision but denies it creates the inverse trend.

reasons.opus: Repeated measurement reduces the imprecision the claim describes.
reasons.sonnet: Says repeated assessment reduces the reporting error.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Repeated assessments reduce the imprecision.

reasons.opus: The prospective design keeps errors from distorting the outcome relationship.
reasons.sonnet: Grants imprecision but says it doesn't create outcome-linked distortion.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Prospective design limits the distortion that matters for the parent.

reasons.opus: Mendelian randomization evidence shows the signal is not a questionnaire artifact.
reasons.sonnet: Grants imprecision but says the signal isn't an artifact of it.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Independent evidence shows the signal is not a questionnaire artifact.

reasons.opus: Imprecise dose does not invalidate cups as the exposure.
reasons.sonnet: Addresses brew strength, a different issue.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Imprecision about dose does not invalidate a cups-based analysis.

reasons.opus: A poor biomarker reference means the discrepancies do not show questionnaire error.
reasons.sonnet: Biomarker is a poor reference so discrepancies don't show error.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Biomarker mismatch does not show questionnaire error.

reasons.opus: Biomarker variability means the mismatch need not reflect questionnaire error.
reasons.sonnet: Biomarker mismatch may reflect metabolism, not questionnaire error.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Biomarker variability, not the questionnaire, may drive the mismatch.

reasons.opus: Biomarkers are invalid references, so the findings do not show questionnaire error.
reasons.sonnet: Biomarker validity limits so discrepancies don't show misclassification.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Biomarkers are invalid reference measures, so the error they reveal is doubtful.

reasons.opus: The validation results may not generalize to the cohorts.
reasons.sonnet: Small samples may not generalize the error.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Grants the error but denies it generalizes to the cohorts.

reasons.opus: Says validation studies find good agreement, not substantial error.
reasons.sonnet: Says validation shows good agreement, not substantial misclassification.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Good agreement contradicts frequent misclassification.

reasons.opus: Calibration corrects the error, so it does not distort the dose-response.
reasons.sonnet: Calibration corrects error so it doesn't explain the association.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Calibration corrects the error before analysis.

reasons.opus: Says the evidence does not establish category misclassification.
reasons.sonnet: Says modest correlation doesn't establish substantial misclassification.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Modest correlation does not show substantial misclassification.

reasons.opus: Random error biases toward the null instead of creating a spurious trend.
reasons.sonnet: Random error biases toward null, not a spurious trend.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Random error would not produce a spurious inverse trend.

reasons.opus: Says breakeven often comes well under five years.
reasons.sonnet: Says costs are recovered well under five years.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Says break-even often comes well under five years.

reasons.opus: Denies a typical five-year recovery period.
reasons.sonnet: Denies a typical five-year recovery period.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Denies there is a typical five-year period.

reasons.opus: Costs can be cut, shortening breakeven below the stated period.
reasons.sonnet: Mitigation possibility, not a denial of the typical case.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: An individual buyer can avoid the typical costs.

reasons.opus: Moving costs apply to renters too, so they do not favor renting.
reasons.sonnet: Says moving costs are overcounted as buying costs.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Moving costs also apply to renting, so they don't favor renting.

reasons.opus: Even with unrecovered costs, buying may still beat renting.
reasons.sonnet: Grants costs but says buying may still beat renting.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Countervailing equity benefit of buying.

reasons.opus: Tax benefits offset costs, so slow appreciation-based breakeven need not favor renting.
reasons.sonnet: Says tax benefits shorten the break-even.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Separate tax benefit offsetting costs.

reasons.opus: Rent savings can offset costs without appreciation.
reasons.sonnet: Other savings offset costs, so the claim doesn't favor renting.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Separate rent-savings benefit.

reasons.opus: Rising rents erode the advantage the claim implies for renting.
reasons.sonnet: Rising rent erases the advantage the costs imply.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Separate cost of renting.

reasons.opus: Possible fast gains are speculative, so they do not undermine the 'typically' claim.
reasons.sonnet: Grants possibility but says it's unreliable as an offset.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Possible fast appreciation is too unreliable to undercut the typical claim.

reasons.opus: Says early principal paydown is too small to help much.
reasons.sonnet: Says principal paydown is too small to offset costs.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Early principal paydown is too small to help.

reasons.opus: Says counting paydown as an offset overstates the gains.
reasons.sonnet: Says paydown isn't a real gain, overstating the offset.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Paydown should not count as an offset.

reasons.opus: Raises other ongoing costs as a countervailing factor.
reasons.sonnet: Adds separate ownership costs.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Countervailing ongoing costs.

reasons.opus: Gains may not be realizable when the move date is fixed.
reasons.sonnet: Timing uncontrollability prevents capturing the gains.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Gains may not be realizable when the move date is fixed.

reasons.opus: A tax bill prevents the gains from actually covering the costs.
reasons.sonnet: Tax bill prevents appreciation from covering costs.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Countervailing tax cost.

reasons.opus: Says expected appreciation is already priced in at purchase.
reasons.sonnet: Says appreciation is already priced in.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Appreciation is already priced in, so the gains are overstated.

reasons.opus: Boom rates are outliers and do not show this is typical or predictable.
reasons.sonnet: Boom rates are unrepresentative and unpredictable.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Outlier booms don't support claims about many markets.

reasons.opus: Taxes erode the gains, so they do not establish faster breakeven.
reasons.sonnet: Taxes erode gains used to justify breakeven.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Countervailing tax cost.

reasons.opus: Metro-wide gains do not carry over to an individual property.
reasons.sonnet: Metro data doesn't ensure an individual property's gains.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Metro-wide figures don't carry over to individual homes.

reasons.opus: Boom gains can reverse before the sale.
reasons.sonnet: Gains may reverse before a forced sale.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Temporary gains may not be there at sale.

reasons.opus: Disputes the claimed 8-10% transaction-cost baseline during booms.
reasons.sonnet: Says true round-trip costs are higher than assumed.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Boom-period transaction costs exceed the cited baseline.

reasons.opus: About buying versus renting overall, not whether gains exceed transaction costs.
reasons.sonnet: Appreciation exceeding costs doesn't show buying beats renting.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Addresses buy vs rent, not the parent's break-even claim.

reasons.opus: Price gains include renovation spending, so they overstate the return.
reasons.sonnet: Renovation-driven gains overstate the return from appreciation.
reasons.opus-adjudicator: Renovation spending inflates the measured equity gains.
